title: platform-objects: System Overview's six metric tiles declare `layout.h: 2` and draw a half-empty box; set them to `h: 1` (ruling B on objectui#12704)
body:
Filed by the director seat (summon #43 continuation 3, `session_01QJC7i981TSs9L1CGJK59Ax`) on the maintainer's ruling B on objectstack-ai/objectui#12704 (batch #358 item 4, 「12704 同意」; the ruling record is that card's `Ruled:` line). ⛔ Not a claim. Filing gate ①: a measured defect in shipped metadata with a named site.

## What is measured (objectstack `origin/main` `be076dad28a0`, objectui `d0a00d795020`)
`packages/platform-objects/src/apps/dashboards/system_overview.dashboard.ts` declares 6 `type: 'metric'` widgets, every one `layout.h: 2`. The console's positioned dashboard grid gives each row a floor of 5rem and spans a widget over the rows its `h` names (`packages/plugin-dashboard/src/DashboardRenderer.tsx`, `gridAutoRows: 'minmax(5rem, auto)'`), and `MetricCard` fills its box (`h-full`), so at 1024 px each tile is about 135 px tall with the title and the number in the top 60 px and an empty lower half (objectui#12704's screenshots). The ruling: the platform draws what the metadata declares — ADR-0078 forbids an `h` that is read and not honoured — so the authored size is corrected, not the renderer.

## Scope
1. The 6 metric tiles go `h: 2` → `h: 1`; the chart widgets (`h: 4`) and every `x`, `y`, `w` stay.
2. No other dashboard, no `packages/spec` change, no renderer change.

## Done when
- The 6 tiles declare `h: 1`; the existing `platform-objects` tests are green.
- `Clause-②: no`; a `patch` changeset for `@objectstack/platform-objects` (shipped metadata changes).
- After objectui's regression pin (objectui#12704, re-scoped by the ruling) lands: System Overview at 1024 and 1280 px shows each metric tile at content height (88–96 px for a bare number).

Related: objectstack-ai/objectui#12704 (the ruling and the objectui pin), the hotcrm sibling card filed in the same act (HotCRM's metric tiles), objectui#12623 (the title on its own line, the precedent).
